message: The document level allowance amount (BT-92) at {@/BT-92} is {/BT-92}, which needs more than two fraction digits; an amount of this standard carries at most two.
note: The number an identifier of this family carries is the official validation artefacts' and not the standard's: clause 6.5.12 states the allowed number of fraction digits per business term in a table and gives the restriction no rule identifier, and the artefacts number one rule per row. The identifier is kept so that a report can be compared with theirs. The statement is about how many fraction digits an amount may carry. An ESJ document has no second spelling of a number — the decimal form of the specification carries no trailing fraction zeros and a value that carries them is refused at layer L2 — so what is counted here is the fraction digits the number needs. An invoice that reached the official artefacts as XML spelling 100.00 counts two digits there and none here; the two answers differ only where the spelling differs from the number, which the ledger records.
